briefs.headline: Hannan's Region IV result against Tug Valley goes unpublished overnight
briefs.summary: No. 10 Tug Valley at No. 7 Hannan, the WVSSAC Class AA-A Region IV first round, was set for 7 p.m. ET Monday at Ashton, and no outlet this paper may cite had a score by 5:46 a.m. ET Tuesday: MaxPreps returned 403 Forbidden, WV MetroNews' sports pages and site search had nothing on Hannan since June, and the Point Pleasant Register's site failed its TLS handshake. The winner plays No. 2 seed Buffalo on Wednesday at 7 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Maddison scores on his return as Tottenham beat Coventry 3-1 for a first league win
briefs.summary: James Maddison, starting for the first time in 536 days, curled a 22-yard opener in the 14th minute Monday in London; Jack Rudoni levelled in the 49th before Omar Marmoush's first Spurs goal in the 58th and Ben Davies' stoppage-time third. Dejan Kulusevski came off the bench after 526 days out, but Adarabioyo, Robertson and Marmoush all limped off; the win lifts Tottenham from 20th to 16th before Saturday's house derby in west London.

briefs.headline: Rays beat Guardians 7-3 in Game 6 to win the ALCS and reach the World Series
briefs.summary: Freddy Peralta threw 5 1/3 innings Monday night at Tropicana Field and Junior Caminero and Yandy Diaz each hit a two-run homer as Tampa Bay closed the series 4-2 for its third World Series in 29 seasons; the Rays led 3-0 after three innings and added two runs in each of the seventh and eighth. Cleveland's title drought reaches 78 years. Game 1 against the Brewers is Friday night in Milwaukee.

briefs.headline: 49ers hold off Commanders 23-17 on Monday night to reach 6-0
briefs.summary: Brock Purdy went 21 of 29 for 264 yards and a touchdown to George Kittle, Christian McCaffrey ran for two 1-yard scores and San Francisco led 23-3 in the third quarter before Jayden Daniels threw two second-half touchdowns; Malik Mustapha broke up a fourth-down pass near the goal line with 1:54 left. Purdy, past 1,500 attempts, became the NFL's highest-rated career passer at 105.6; Washington is 1-4-1.

briefs.headline: UCLA's Iamaleava needs season-ending knee surgery after the Oregon win
briefs.summary: Coach Bob Chesney said Monday the quarterback's injury from the Oct. 10 win over then-No. 13 Oregon is severe and that surgery would follow Monday or Tuesday; Ty Dieffenbach, who went 22 of 33 for 264 yards in Saturday's win over Wisconsin, takes over for the unbeaten Bruins against Michigan State on Saturday.

briefs.headline: Auburn dismisses linebacker Xavier Atkins after suspending him for the Georgia upset
briefs.summary: Sources told ESPN on Monday night that Auburn dismissed the first-team All-SEC linebacker, who led the league with 17 tackles for loss in 2025 and had been suspended, for an undisclosed reason, before Saturday's win over then-No. 1 Georgia; coach Alex Golesh had said earlier Monday the matter was still being worked through.

briefs.headline: Kyushu basho opens Nov. 8 in Fukuoka, 19 days out, with the banzuke due Monday
briefs.summary: The Japan Sumo Association's tournament schedule page lists the November tournament, the Kyushu basho (tournament), for Nov. 8 to 22 at the Fukuoka Kokusai Center, with the banzuke (rankings) announced Monday, Oct. 26. Tuesday's sweep of the JSA, Japan Times, Nikkan Sports, Hochi, Nippon.com, Mainichi and NHK turned up no new sumo news.

prime.item: Day 6. Proclamation SF-1-2026, signed Oct. 2 by Division of Marine Fisheries interim director Michael S. Loeffler and re-opened this morning at 5:44 a.m. by its files.nc.gov address (HTTP 200, PDF, pdftotext), made the hand harvest of oysters from public bottom in internal coastal fishing waters effective at sunrise Thursday, Oct. 15, and says the season closes March 31, 2027, under Marine Fisheries Commission rule 15A NCAC 03K .0201 unless closed sooner by proclamation. The recreational limit it sets for unlicensed persons and harvesters taking oysters for personal consumption is one bushel per person per day, not to exceed two bushels per vessel per day, seven days a week, from public bottom; it is unlawful to take oysters between sunset and sunrise, or from the oyster sanctuaries designated in rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117. The division's proclamations index, all six pages read at 5:44 a.m., lists SF-1-2026 as issued Oct. 2 and effective at sunrise Oct. 15 and carries nothing issued after Oct. 15; NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened at 5:44 a.m. and still dated effective Sept. 2, 2026, reads oysters as season closed, unlawful to possess, while its own footnote reads oyster season is Oct. 15 to March 31 unless closed earlier by proclamation, and the proclamation is the later document. Topsail Sound is coastal water under the Division of Marine Fisheries.

NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened this morning at 5:44 a.m. with a browser user agent and dated effective Sept. 2, 2026, lists red drum at an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length and one per day, under federal red drum management, with a footnote that it is unlawful to possess red drum over 27 inches or to gig, spear or gaff them; the division's flounder proclamation FF-27-2026, which the page links and which was re-read this morning with pdftotext, cites Marine Fisheries Commission rule 15A NCAC 3I .0124 requiring recreational anglers to report red drum, spotted seatrout, flounder, striped bass and weakfish harvest to the division. The proclamations index, all six pages read at 5:44 a.m., carries no 2026 recreational red drum proclamation and nothing issued after Oct. 15. Topsail Sound is coastal water under the Division of Marine Fisheries, and the limits page says a Coastal Recreational Fishing License is required in coastal waters under G.S. 113-174.2, a separate license from the inland one. The Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 19 days old, has red drum as the main inshore target around Topsail.

prime.dates: Open; 14- to 20-inch slot, one over 26 inches
prime.item: NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning, lists spotted seatrout, the speckled trout, at a 14- to 20-inch total-length slot with one fish over 26 inches allowed, three per day, no federal regulation. The division's proclamations index, read at 5:44 a.m., lists the harvest opening as FF-31-2026, issued June 25 and effective 12:01 a.m. July 1, 2026, and carries no later seatrout proclamation; the October proclamations on the index are the oyster opening, three commercial flounder orders (FF-42, FF-43 and FF-44-2026, the latest issued Oct. 15), and gill net and other gear orders (M-21 through M-24-2026, issued Oct. 2 and Oct. 9). The Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 19 days old, has the trout scattered, a few on early topwater, the guides waiting on cooler water; Beaufort's thermometer read 63.3 degrees this morning, down 1.6 from Monday's 64.9.

prime.species: Spanish mackerel, king mackerel and bluefish
prime.item: NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning, lists Spanish mackerel at 12 inches fork length and 15 per day, king mackerel at 24 inches fork length and three per day, and bluefish with no minimum size and five per day in private recreational fisheries, seven on a for-hire vessel, all under federal management plans. The Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 19 days old, has Spanish and bluefish plentiful from the surf and piers and kings to 32 pounds at Jolly Roger Pier.

NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning, lists black drum at a 14-inch minimum and 25-inch maximum total length, 10 per day, with one over 25 inches allowed per person per day, sheepshead at 14 inches total length, five per day, neither under federal regulation, and spot with no minimum size and 50 per day under federal spot management. The reference calendar lists October as the peak of the spot run; the Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 19 days old, has black drum of three to four pounds at the bridges and oyster reefs, spot in the evening bottom-fishing catch at Surf City Pier and sheepshead in the Seaview Pier bottom catch.

going_out.dates: Harvest Sept. 1 to 14 only; closed since Sept. 15
going_out.item: Closed. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened this morning at 5:44 a.m., reads flounder, all species, Sept. 1 to 14 open and Sept. 15 to 30 closed, unlawful to possess, and carries no October opening; the proclamation it links, FF-27-2026, which the server delivered as a PDF (HTTP 200) and which was re-read this morning with pdftotext, was signed June 3 by director Kathy B. Rawls and says it is unlawful to possess flounder for recreational purposes except from 12:01 a.m. Sept. 1 until 11:59 p.m. Sept. 14, 2026, with a 15-inch minimum and one per person per day inside that window, supersedes FF-17-2026 of March 13 and sets no later season; the division's proclamations index, all six pages read at 5:44 a.m., lists three October flounder proclamations, FF-42-2026 issued Oct. 6, FF-43-2026 issued Oct. 13 and FF-44-2026 issued Oct. 15, all commercial pound net and mobile gear orders, nothing issued after Oct. 15, and no recreational one. Flounder in Topsail Sound are release only, the 36th day of the closure; the Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 19 days old, has them as bycatch on red drum rigs and in the pier bottom-fishing catch.

waters.read: 324 cfs - pushy. Wadeable at the edges, not across.
waters.working: Down 97 on the day, still falling, and under the 358 cfs it bottomed at Wednesday evening before Thursday's rise, cited from Sunday's edition, so this is the lowest the river has read since before that rise. The read string is the fetcher's own verdict, "324 cfs - pushy. Wadeable at the edges, not across.", and the band is right: the fetcher's pushy band runs 200 to 500 cfs and the river is 124 above the 200-cfs line and 176 under the blown-out line it crossed at 4 p.m. Sunday. The 582 cfs and 3.08 feet in the fetcher's 24h_ago fields are the first points of its two-day window, the 5:30 and 5:45 a.m. Sunday readings, about 47.5 hours before the current reading, and the USGS 03186500 trace pulled at 5:45 a.m. puts the true 24-hour mark at 421 cfs and 2.73 feet at 5:15 a.m. Monday, Monday's edition reading, so the river is down 97 cfs and 0.25 feet on the day, not the 258 cfs and 0.60 feet the comparison implies; the falling flag is right on the day either way. The recession ran straight through Monday with no bump: 421 cfs at 5:15 a.m., 417 at 6, 409 at 7, 405 at 8 and 9, 397 at 10, 393 at 11, 389 at noon, 385 at 1 p.m., 381 at 2 and 3, 373 at 4, 369 at 5, 365 at 6, 361 at 7, 358 at 8, 354 at 9, 350 at 10 and 11, 343 at midnight, 339 at 1 a.m., 335 at 2, 332 at 3, 328 at 4 and 4:30, 324 at 4:45, 5 and 5:15 a.m., the last point on the trace and the window low; stage went 2.73 Monday morning to 2.48. The rate of fall held at about 4 cfs an hour all day and overnight, and at that rate the 200-cfs line, where the long-leader, small-fly water begins, is about 27 hours off, longer as the recession slows, an arithmetic note and not a forecast. The window high is 587 cfs and 3.09 feet at 5 and 5:15 a.m. Sunday. The Gauley near Craigsville (03189100), above Summersville Lake, read 1,330 cfs and 12.05 feet at 4:30 a.m., the last point on its trace, against 1,700 cfs and 12.34 feet at 4:30 a.m. Monday, the true 24-hour mark, down 370 on the day, 10 to 20 cfs an hour. 03189600 below Summersville Dam, stage only, its discharge series again carrying no values, a tenth day (the service's latest discharge value is dated Sept. 30, 2003), finished Monday morning's drop: 9.83 feet at 4:45 a.m. Monday, 9.21 at 5, 8.71 at 6, 8.50 at 7, 8.31 at 8, 7.83 at 9 and 7.78 at 10 a.m., then flat between 7.76 and 7.78 for 19 hours, 7.76 at 4:45 a.m. today, 3.27 feet under the 11.03 it held at 2 a.m. Monday, a reading off a USGS stage trace and not a Corps statement; the Corps' Huntington District site was not opened and no release figure is printed. At 324 cfs and falling the Williams is still a heavy-nymph-on-the-seam river, closer to the edges-only problem than Monday's 421: the pocket water, plunge pools and undercut banks the file records as its structure are showing again at the margins, the middle is not crossable, which is the fetcher's wadeable-at-the-edges line. Stoneflies and caddis are the forage the file records, so a weighted stonefly nymph, size 6 to 8, on point with a caddis pupa dropper, under an indicator or on a tight line, worked up the inside seams and the soft water inside each plunge pool's tail-out from the near bank, with less split shot than Monday needed; sculpin are the third forage, so an olive or black weighted sculpin pattern on a sink tip swung along the undercut banks and through the plunge pools where the current drops off, which fishes better as the water clears on a recession this steady. The fetcher carries no Williams water temperature, so none is printed. WVDNR's trout stocking page was not opened today; no stocking line is printed.

waters.working: Two days past the quarter and building toward the full: the fetcher's file carries the moon as waxing gibbous, 67 percent lit and 9.0 days old, and the U.S. Naval Observatory's phase table, which answered at 5:46 a.m., puts the first quarter at 16:12 UT Sunday, 12:12 p.m. ET, the full moon at 04:12 UT Oct. 26, 12:12 a.m. ET next Monday, and the last quarter at 20:28 UT Nov. 1, so the neap is behind and the swings grow each day this week toward the spring tides, harder current through the inlet and more bait moving on the tide; today's sound range is 2.9 feet on the afternoon flood against Monday's 2.9, and the surf's 3.2 against Monday's 3.0. NWS Wilmington has one product on the water this morning and nothing on the beach at Topsail. The Small Craft Advisory for the coastal waters from Surf City to Cape Fear out 20 nautical miles (AMZ250, also AMZ252), the marine zone off the beach and the inlet, was reissued at 1:36 a.m. today: north winds 15 to 25 knots and seas 4 to 7 feet until 6 p.m. Wednesday, Oct. 21, conditions the Service calls hazardous to small craft, a marine product for the ocean out 20 miles and not a sound product; the seas are down from Monday's 7 to 10 feet and the gusts-to-30 line is gone, and the end time moved from 8 a.m. Wednesday to 6 p.m. Wednesday. Coastal Pender (NCZ106), the Topsail zone, carried no active product at 5:44 a.m.: Monday's Rip Current Statement expired at 8 p.m. and nothing replaced it; the next county south, Coastal New Hanover (NCZ108), has a High Surf Advisory to 8 a.m. and a Rip Current Statement to 8 p.m. today, 4- to 6-foot breakers and a strong north-to-south longshore current, which stop at the county line and are not printed as Topsail's. All four sound events fall inside Tuesday this morning and none carries a spillover tag: the sound at Hampstead topped out at 3.3 feet at 3:47 a.m., is on its ebb at press time, draining 2.4 feet to a 0.9-foot low at 10:09 a.m., then fills 2.9 feet to a 3.8-foot high at 4:21 p.m. and drains 2.8 feet to a 1.0-foot low at 10:53 p.m.; the last two hours of the evening ebb, about 9 to 10:53 p.m., run in the dark, with sunset before 6:30, an approximation not from the fetcher. The surf at Ocean City Beach pier runs ahead and is the bigger water: high 3:17 a.m. at 3.6, low 9:08 a.m. at 1.2, high 3:42 p.m. at 4.4 and low 10:06 p.m. at 1.1, a 3.2-foot flood and a 3.3-foot ebb against Monday's 3.0 each way. Today's lags from the two tables are 30 and 39 minutes on the highs and 61 and 47 minutes on the lows; the morning low again lags longest, the shallow sound draining slower than it fills, which stretches the drum window at the crew's spot past what a flat offset would give. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, read 63.3 degrees at 5:30 a.m., down 1.6 from Monday's 64.9 and 13.7 from Saturday's 77.0, the earlier figures cited from the week's editions, the third morning of the north wind; the fetcher's file gives no reading at Topsail itself. What is running is 19 days old, not a month: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report posted Thursday, Oct. 1, at 9 a.m. ET, and the feed carried it as its newest item at 5:44 this morning. East Coast Sports has slot red drum with over-slots mixed in off the surf and piers, Spanish and bluefish plentiful, kings showing more at the piers, trolled spoons working off the beach, and inshore red drum as the main target, scattered over the ICW, the creeks and the inlets, with no word on trout yet; Native Son has mullet everywhere and reds at the docks, creek mouths and grass lines, trout scattered on early topwater, glass minnows thick off the beach and the kings still in 50 to 60 feet; Spring Tide has the reds schooled in the bays at 22 to 28 inches and better, topwater and artificials some days and cut bait others, trout quiet until the water cools, Spanish pushing inside the inlet on the high tide; Speckled Specialist has Carolina-rigged live mullet the best red drum bait, trout in the first hour of light on Spook Jr. topwaters and then live shrimp under slip corks in 15 to 20 feet, black drum of three to four pounds at the bridges and oyster reefs on shrimp; Carolina Flats has big mullet moving into the ICW and the bigger reds on live finger mullet or Gulp soft plastics under popping corks, flounder as bycatch, false albacore due on the nearshore structure; Plan 9 has Spanish of 14 to 22 inches and false albacore just outside the inlet in 15 to 20 feet on small metal and epoxy jigs; South End has the bigger Spanish in 45 to 50 feet over hard bottom under feeding birds and kings in the 8- to 12-mile range. The piers: Jolly Roger reports bait thick, multiple kings to 32 pounds, Spanish ramping up, and night bottom fishing producing red drum to 31 inches, Virginia mullet, pompano, bluefish, black drum and some flounder; Surf City Pier has good-sized Spanish on Gotcha plugs, slot and occasional over-slot reds, and evening bottom fishing with black drum, mullet, spot and croaker; Seaview Pier has the mullet migration starting, Spanish and bluefish on Gotcha plugs and diamond jigs, and a bottom mixed bag of flounder, sea mullet, spot, sheepshead, trout, black drum and the odd red. The reference calendar's October pattern, spot at peak, red drum, trout, bluefish, sea mullet and black drum, matches the report. On today's tides and this water, a tide problem before it is a lure problem, and still a wind problem: the advisory's north wind is on the ocean, and in the sound a north wind blows down the ICW, holds water out of the creeks on the ebb and lays the lee on the mainland shore. The sound is on its morning ebb until 10:09 a.m., an hour later than Monday's, and the last two hours of it, about 8 to 10:09 a.m., are the red drum stage and fall in full daylight after the first hour of light, finger mullet the forage the file records and the report says the mullet are in, so a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig or a three-inch Gulp shrimp under a popping cork fan-cast a couple of feet off the channel edge where the creek mouths drain the grass, a cut mullet chunk on the bottom at the same edge as the water gets low, from the lee bank; the report's first-hour topwater for trout, a Spook Jr. walked over the deeper grass edges, falls earlier, on the middle of the ebb this morning. The flood from 10:09 a.m. to 4:21 p.m. covers the oyster bars and grass edges, mud minnows and shrimp the forage there, so a quarter-ounce gold spoon or a paddletail on a three-sixteenths-ounce head along the grass edges and across the oyster bars as they go under, and a live shrimp on a slip cork at the oyster bars and the bridge pilings for the black drum and sheepshead, the report's three- to four-pounders. The 4:21 p.m. high puts 3.8 feet of water over the grass and up the dock pilings, where the reds go on a flooded high, so a topwater walked over the grass edges and down the dock lines on the last of the flood, about 2:30 to 4:21 p.m., then a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig as the ebb starts. The red drum window proper is the bottom of the evening ebb, roughly 9 to 10:53 p.m., 49 minutes later than Monday's and in the dark, the same Carolina-rigged mullet and cut mullet at the channel edges; with Beaufort down 13.7 degrees in three mornings, the cool-down the guides in the report say the trout are waiting on is on the thermometer, so a live shrimp under a slip cork in the deeper holes, 15 to 20 feet, on the first of the evening ebb, and the dock lights after the 10:53 p.m. low. Oysters are in their sixth day open under SF-1-2026 on the public bottom; the oyster bars the crew fishes over are the same structure, and the sanctuaries in rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117 are closed to harvest. The surf side is under the Small Craft Advisory's 15 to 25 knots of north wind and 4 to 7 feet of sea on the water out 20 miles through Wednesday evening, with no beach product at Topsail today; the piers' Gotcha-plug Spanish bite on the flood to the 3:42 p.m. high, 4.4 feet at the pier, and the evening cut-bait session for slot reds fall inside it. Slack at 10:09 a.m., 4:21 p.m. and 10:53 p.m. is dead water. Flounder are release only, the 36th day.
